name: Seller Snap
summary: AI repricer and seller-analytics platform for Amazon and Walmart — what the vendor calls game-theory repricing, aimed at Buy Box share rather than racing to the bottom, plus min/max profit calculation, 80+ analytics data points and imports from tools like InventoryLab and SkuVault. 15-day free trial, no credit card. A July 2026 interface release adds live Buy Box insight with SKU-level filters, multi-store management from one screen including bulk cost updates, repricing from mobile, historical inventory-value tracking, saved views, customizable columns and a dark mode.
best_for: Amazon and Walmart sellers past the hobby stage who compete for the Buy Box on a catalog of up to a few thousand SKUs, and want AI repricing and deep seller analytics in one place. The 15-day no-card trial makes it cheap to test against your own listings before any commitment
skip_if: you sell mainly outside Amazon and Walmart, since those are the only two marketplaces supported. Also skip it if your catalog and revenue are small enough that a rules-based repricer at a fraction of the price does the same job, or if what you actually need is multi-channel competitor price monitoring rather than marketplace Buy Box repricing
honest_knock: Read the caps before you read the prices, because the caps are what you are actually buying. Two of them deserve scrutiny. First, the revenue limits — $15,000 on Starter, $30,000 on Accelerator. Until September the pricing page printed them with no period attached; we asked, and Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both caps are calculated per month, which is how the page has printed them since ('Up to $15K/mo revenue'). That is the reading that costs you money. $15,000 a month is roughly $500 a day, so a seller who already clears that sits above Starter before signing up — and $30,000 a month puts the ceiling of Accelerator within reach of a shop doing $1,000 a day. Measure your own monthly revenue against the tier first, because the page will not do it for you. Second, the SKU limit sits at 1,000 on both of the lower tiers, so catalog growth alone — not revenue, not users — can push you up a step. And the steps are steep: leaving Accelerator for Standard means $425/month annually or $500 monthly, roughly twice what you were paying, for capacity rather than for any feature you did not already have. The cheapest door is also not quite $100: Starter is annual-billing only, so the lowest month-to-month entry into the product is $250/month. Finally, the annual Accelerator rate rose from $175 to $212 a month between our September and October readings while the monthly rate stayed at $250, so confirm the figure on the page the day you sign rather than one from a screenshot. Worth checking first, though: Amazon already includes a rule-based repricer. Automate Pricing comes with the Professional selling plan and supports rules such as Competitive Featured Offer and Competitive Lowest Price with a seller-set price floor, so if your problem is simply matching the competitive price without going below cost, test that before paying for anything. And note what sets your tier: their FAQ says pricing follows the total number of SKUs in your Seller Central account, not the active ones, so a dormant catalogue costs you money. One more thing to time correctly. In September 2026 Seller Snap began telling affiliates that its most advanced repricing engine yet had just launched, built on the premise that Amazon no longer awards one Buy Box but thousands of local ones, buyer by buyer and city by city. Their own repricing-engine page, read on 3 Sep 2026, is more careful than that: it says a redesigned app today, a new repricing engine coming soon, and it offers a waitlist and an early-access form rather than the engine itself. What has actually shipped is the redesigned app — a live Buy Box filter at SKU level, one preset across every store, repricing from a phone, and historical inventory value tracked over time. The local Buy Box logic sits behind that, still ahead of the product rather than in it. So judge the subscription on what the app does today; if the local pricing engine is the reason you are signing up, ask support for a ship date in writing before you pay for a year of it.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-07 on their own pricing page, both the monthly and the annual column) There are four tiers, and the axis that sets your price is capacity, not features. Starter is $100 a month on annual billing only: 1,000 SKUs, one marketplace, one user and up to $15K a month in revenue. Accelerator is $250 month to month or $212 a month paid annually, billed $2,544 a year: the same 1,000 SKUs, three users, up to $30K a month in revenue, and it adds Walmart, Amazon Business B2B repricing and an onboarding specialist. Standard is $500 month to month or $425 a month paid annually, billed $5,100 a year: 15,000 SKUs, three users, no revenue cap, a dedicated account manager and multi-store support. Custom, above Standard, is quote-only. The annual Accelerator rate went up between our September and October readings: it was $175 a month with a $900 yearly saving, and it is now $212 with a saving the page puts at $446 (its own figures give $456). The monthly rates and both Standard figures did not move, so annual billing now takes about 15 percent off Accelerator and Standard alike, where it used to take 30 percent off the smaller plan. What each step buys is still lopsided: Accelerator doubles your revenue ceiling and leaves the SKU count alone, and Standard does the reverse — fifteen times the catalogue with the ceiling removed. So the middle tier is for turnover and the top tier is for range, and a shop that needs neither is paying for the other one. The page now prints the revenue ceilings per month ('Up to $15K/mo revenue'), which matches what Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026. Walmart is no longer on every plan: the Accelerator card reads 'Everything in Starter, plus Walmart, B2B repricing and onboarding specialist'. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card. Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that readers coming through our link get 10% off for their first three months; it runs through the link, there is no code to enter. The banner offering a first month for $1 'when you subscribe before 2026', which we flagged as expired in August, was still in our 1 October capture but is gone from the page we read on 7 October.

compare_with.name: Feedvisor
compare_with.why: the other AI-first Amazon repricer we cover: Feedvisor's real platform (Feedvisor360, with ad optimization and dedicated analysts) starts around $1,500/mo, while Seller Snap sits in the $100-$500/mo band on published, self-serve pricing with a no-card trial. If you need multi-channel price monitoring rather than marketplace repricing, compare Pricefy instead — and verify every current price list yourself before you sign.
